title: NG1: Sufficiency of the characterization (Thm 1) is under-proven / false for same-edge internal pairs

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, proof of Theorem 1 (Characterization), Case B, the subcase "if q lies on e" (lines 166-179).

**The gap.** Condition (G) is *defined only for vertices q that do NOT lie on e* (Definition, lines 102-109). Therefore (G) gives no constraint on a pair p,q both internal to the SAME edge e=ab, and the sufficiency proof must obtain uniqueness for such pairs from (U) alone. The text (lines 169-179) asserts the direct sub-segment of e of length |r-r| is "the unique shortest p-q path," but this is false in a regime (U) permits:

- Distance from a to a point of e at offset r is min(r, R(a,b)+(x_e - r)), where R(a,b) is the least weight of an H-path a->b NOT using e. (U) only requires the *minimum-weight* a-b path to be unique; that minimum may be the wrap-around of weight R(a,b) rather than e itself. If x_e > R(a,b), the direct segment need not be shortest at all: a wrap-around p->a->(ext)->b->q can be strictly shorter. The claimed conclusion then collapses.
- The truncation argument (lines 175-179) does not enumerate the case where an external path leaves and returns to the SAME endpoint, and never establishes uniqueness of the wrap-around shortest path when the wrap-around IS the geodesic. The bound min over xi,eta of (dist_p(xi)+R(xi,eta)+dist_q(eta)) is written but never rigorously compared to |r-r|.

**Consequence.** Theorem 1 is the central result; Algorithm correctness, the infiniteness corollary, and every downstream claim depend on it. As written its sufficiency proof has a genuine hole.

**To close.** Supply a rigorous same-edge lemma: for p,q on e at offsets r<r, compute d_{G}(p,q) as the min of the direct segment (r-r) and all wrap-arounds r+R(a,b)+(x_e-r) etc., and prove the minimizer is UNIQUE, reducing every tie to a violation of (U) (two min-weight a-b H-paths) or to a branch-level (G) tie. Handle x_e<=R(a,b) and x_e>R(a,b) separately. Alternatively, extend the quantifier in (G) to include same-edge targets and re-derive necessity.
